name: jitter-and-unknown
description: Four cells, 80 epochs each. jitter aims the head per frame, lifting query viewpoint spread from 3.7 to 21.4 degrees, and implies the loss mask since it drops the answerable fraction from 77% to 58%. unknown turns on both halves of the unknown-space work together: an observedness channel on the volume, and a KL weighted per latent voxel by how much of its region was seen. jitter=0 unknown=0 is the baseline that anchors the sweep. 80 rather than 40 epochs because no run has ever gone past 40 and this model reads 0.645 at 6 epochs against 0.277 at 15 -- late signal is the norm here, and no run has yet produced a good render. Judge the unknown axis on val/lift_agreement_best with val/invented_density beside it, since an empty volume wins invention outright. The jitter axis is not settled by any single number -- it changes the task, so image-space metrics penalise the masked side and volume-space ones face a different lift target. Read the sweep/scene* figures for that one. adaptive rather than onecycle: the sweep that preferred onecycle tested an adaptive with no warmup, which no longer exists, and adaptive is the only schedule that can be extended -- it holds rate in reserve, so --resume continues mid-slope and --taper ends it, which matters when 'not trained long enough' is the live hypothesis. See .agents/learned.md before changing metrics or adding early termination.
